purpose: On Linux (native TLS, one C runtime) measure what the BridgeStan path costs per gradient call on each dispatch path the shipped crate exposes, the fault rate of each path over 500 child processes, and oWALNUTS-via-BridgeStan wall per gradient against CmdStan 2.39.0 on the fixed-16 posteriordb models; decide under a frozen rule whether the off-Windows concurrent-replica dispatch (and the STAN_THREADS single-module dispatch) is qualified in the README.
wp_number_rule: Highest WP in README evidence list and wiki ledger at freeze: WP63. Lane 1 takes WP64; this study is WP65.
source_commit_note: main at freeze (a49df800). The study adds files only under STUDIES/bridgestan_linux_dispatch_v1; run_bench.py refuses oWALNUTS cells if src/, integrations/, tests/ or Cargo.toml differ from this commit.

dispatch_paths_exposed_off_windows.DirectSerialised: StanTarget on a library built without STAN_THREADS: one module, every native call under one module mutex. The Linux analogue of the Windows owned-worker serialisation (the owned worker itself and the process-global native-call lock are cfg(windows) only).
dispatch_paths_exposed_off_windows.DirectConcurrent: StanTarget on a STAN_THREADS=true library: one module called concurrently by every sampler thread.
dispatch_paths_exposed_off_windows.ReplicatedConcurrent: ReplicatedStanTarget::load(.., n > 1): replica 0 at the original path, replicas 1..n-1 as byte copies in the temp dir, free-replica try_lock dispatch. This is what ReplicatedStanTarget::load does off Windows by default, and what posteriordb v7's harness loads.
dispatch_paths_exposed_off_windows.not_exposed: There is no Linux owned-worker path and no separate multi-worker owned path; 'multi-worker' on Linux is ReplicatedConcurrent.

environment.host: AWS EC2 c7a.4xlarge (16 dedicated AMD EPYC 9R14 cores, no SMT, 32 GB, two L3 instances of 32 MB), Ubuntu 24.04, instance i-05c712c79c74ae7f8, us-east-2
environment.lane: lane 2, cores 4-7; every process (builds, drivers, children, CmdStan) runs under taskset -c 4-7; RAYON_NUM_THREADS=4, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, TMPDIR=~/lanes/bridgestan_linux_dispatch_v1/tmp (replica copies are written there)
environment.timing_label: pinned, co-tenanted: the box runs three other core-pinned lanes at the same time (lane 1 on cores 0-3 shares this lane's L3 instance; all lanes share memory bandwidth). Wall-clock and latency numbers are pinned, co-tenanted figures; ESS per gradient, pass counts, fault counts and bit-identity are unaffected by co-tenancy.
environment.toolchain: Rust 1.88.0 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, ~/.cargo from bootstrap), cargo build --release -j4 under taskset; g++ 13.3.0 (Ubuntu 24.04), GNU make
environment.bridgestan: BridgeStan 2.9.0 source release tarball (sha256 b6034f83fb2ffb71ce7be9525b7dded1a225e9a4eaf4b75d4c7e97e3ade05a4c), extracted twice in the lane: bs-nothreads/ and bs-threads/, so the two builds share no objects; default flags (O=3); the shared ~/.bridgestan is not used
environment.cmdstan: CmdStan 2.39.0: a byte copy (cp -a) of ~/infra/cmdstan/cmdstan-2.39.0 in the lane, so model compiles cannot write into the shared tree; cmdstanpy 1.3.0 defaults
environment.python: lane venv: the exact package set of ~/venv (pip freeze; arviz 0.23.4, bridgestan 2.9.0, cmdstanpy 1.3.0, numpy 2.5.4) plus posteriordb 0.2.0, which ~/venv lacks

builds.nothreads: make -C bs-nothreads/bridgestan-2.9.0 <abs>/models/nothreads/<model>_model.so (no STAN_THREADS; the v7 build)

seeds.verified_unused: git grep -n -w -E '65201[0-9]{3}|652651|6529900[0-9]' over every tracked file of the worktree at a49df800 found no occurrence before freezing.

part_a_latency.order: repeat-major: for repeat 1..5, for model in the listed order, for build nothreads then threads; one process at a time

paths_per_process.raw1: raw bs_log_density_gradient function pointer on a model constructed in the process, one caller
paths_per_process.direct4: the same StanTarget, four callers (DirectSerialised for nothreads, DirectConcurrent for threads)
paths_per_process.replicated1: ReplicatedStanTarget with four replicas, one caller

part_a_latency.calls: every caller makes the same number of calls, calibrated once per process from 400 raw calls so that a one-caller path takes about 1 s (clamped to 2,000..4,000,000), over a fixed cycle of 64 positions uniform(-0.5, 0.5) from seed 65299001; caller k starts at position 16k; callers start together at a barrier
part_a_latency.statistics: per (model, build, path): median over the 5 processes of wall per call per caller (us), aggregate wall per gradient (us) and gradients per second; ratios are ratios of those medians

A1.statement: STAN_THREADS costs little on Linux: raw1 latency threads / nothreads <= 1.25 on each of the three models (Windows mingw: 9-16x). Point predictions: eight schools 1.15, arK 1.05, diamonds 1.05.

A2.statement: Replicas scale: nothreads replicated4 / direct4 gradient throughput >= 3.0 on each model. Point: 3.7 on each.

A3.statement: One STAN_THREADS module scales: threads direct4 / nothreads direct4 throughput >= 2.5 on each model. Point: 3.4.

A4.statement: The Rust wrapper and the replica dispatch are cheap: direct1 / raw1 and replicated1 / direct1 latency <= 1.15 on every model and build. Point: <= 1.05.

part_b_fault_rate.run_shape: 4 chains, 4 sampler threads, 1,000 warmup / 1,000 retained, Init::uniform() starts, Metric::diagonal(), Adaptation::default(), Tuning::default(), Limits::new().admit_worst_case(); the model seed passed to BridgeStan is the child seed
part_b_fault_rate.order: paired seeds; for the i-th seed (0-based) the three arms run in the order rotated by i mod 3 (serialised, replicated, threaded_direct); strictly one child at a time
part_b_fault_rate.launch_rule: an exclusive launch marker is created before each child; a launched child is never relaunched; a marker without a process record counts as a fault (interruption)
part_b_fault_rate.manipulation_check: run_stress.py probe loads each arm at seed 65299002 without sampling and must report the expected execution and effective replica count before the matrix may run
part_b_fault_rate.fault_definition: a child is a fault if any of: return code != 0 (including death by signal, e.g. SIGSEGV or SIGABRT from glibc heap checks); timeout; missing or unparsable output; output status != ok; execution label or effective replica count not as expected; any non-finite retained value; retained draw count != 4,000; heartbeat sequence not exactly the twelve expected boundaries; stderr containing any registered marker
part_b_fault_rate.statistics: per path: faults / children, exact one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson upper bound (0/500 gives 0.597%), fault kinds; FNV-1a draw fingerprint and target-call parity serialised vs replicated per seed (same library bytes); serialised vs threaded_direct parity reported (different build); median sampling wall per child reported (descriptive, pinned co-tenanted)

B1.statement: 0 faults on every path: serialised 0/500, replicated 0/500, threaded_direct 0/500 (the Windows record had STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION at drop on the unserialised dynamic-runtime path, 2/120 and 4/300; Linux has native TLS and one C runtime).

B2.statement: serialised and replicated give bit-identical draw fingerprints and identical target-call counts on all 500 seeds.

reported.statement: serialised vs threaded_direct parity (different library build) is reported, not gated; expected identical.

part_c_wall_per_gradient.driver: run_bench.py (a copy of STUDIES/posteriordb_bench_v7/run_posteriordb.py, parametrised); harness src/main.rs (a copy of the v7 harness with a dispatch argument)

owalnuts.role: the Linux default path and v7's exact target call: ReplicatedStanTarget::load(.., 4) -> ReplicatedConcurrent

owalnuts-serialised.role: StanTarget shared by four sampler threads -> DirectSerialised; the Linux analogue of v7's Windows OwnedSerialised path

owalnuts-threaded.role: StanTarget on the STAN_THREADS=true library -> DirectConcurrent

part_c_wall_per_gradient.cmdstan: CmdStan 2.39.0 via cmdstanpy 1.3.0 defaults (adapt_delta 0.8, max_treedepth 10, diag_e, uniform(-2,2) inits, four chains, four parallel chains, no STAN_THREADS), as v7
part_c_wall_per_gradient.sampler_settings: owalnuts::sampler::Sampler::new() with only warmup 1000, draws 1000, chains 4, seed, threads 4 and Limits::new().admit_worst_case(): the commit's default metric, adaptation, tuning and Init (best_of(16)), as v7
part_c_wall_per_gradient.run_order: models in the listed order; per model cmdstan, owalnuts, owalnuts-serialised, owalnuts-threaded; strictly sequential, one sampling process (CmdStan: its four chain processes) at a time

metrics.gradients_total: oWALNUTS target calls including start search, warmup and sampling; CmdStan sum n_leapfrog__ including warmup (v7)
metrics.wall: seconds around one sampler call, warmup included, compilation excluded, oWALNUTS start search excluded; CmdStan process launch and CSV I/O included (v7)
metrics.geomeans: geometric mean over models of per-model ratios, over models whose cells are status ok on both sides (v7 ratio_geomean with one seed)
metrics.gates_and_ess: v7 metrics(): ArviZ 0.23.4 rank R-hat, bulk and tail ESS, reference z; reported, not decisive here (one seed)

C1.statement: On the Linux default (replicated) path the Windows gap disappears: fixed-16 geomean wall per gradient owalnuts / CmdStan <= 1.0 (Windows serialised v7: 1.85x; Windows unserialised v6: 0.825x). Point prediction 0.85.

C2.statement: The serialised Linux path keeps a gap: owalnuts-serialised / CmdStan >= 1.5. Point prediction 2.3 (larger than Windows' contended 1.85x, because pinned CmdStan gets four uncontended cores while serialised gradients use one).

C3.statement: Serialisation costs 1.8x-4.0x sampling wall per gradient: owalnuts-serialised / owalnuts geomean in [1.8, 4.0]. Point 2.7.

C4.statement: owalnuts and owalnuts-serialised are bit-identical (unconstrained draws SHA-256 and gradient count) on all 16 models.

C5.statement: No oWALNUTS cell errors or times out in any of the three arms (48/48 ok).

C6.statement: One STAN_THREADS module is a viable alternative: owalnuts-threaded / owalnuts wall per gradient geomean <= 1.25. Point 1.05.

predictions.reported: threaded vs replicated bit-identity (different build; expected identical), min bulk ESS per gradient vs CmdStan (one seed), pass counts /16 per arm

decision_rule.replicated_qualified_on_linux: ReplicatedConcurrent (ReplicatedStanTarget::load with more than one replica off Windows) is QUALIFIED on Linux x86_64 glibc if all hold: Q1 part (b) replicated 0 faults in 500 counted children; Q2 part (b) serialised-replicated parity 500/500 and part (c) C4 16/16; Q3 faster: part (a) nothreads replicated4/direct4 throughput >= 2.0 on every one of the three models and part (c) owalnuts-serialised/owalnuts wall per gradient geomean >= 1.5; Q4 part (c) owalnuts arm 16/16 cells ok. Otherwise it stays UNQUALIFIED and the README names the failed clause.
decision_rule.threaded_direct_qualified_on_linux: DirectConcurrent (StanTarget on a STAN_THREADS=true library) is QUALIFIED on Linux if: T1 part (b) threaded_direct 0 faults in 500; T2 part (a) threads direct4 / nothreads direct4 throughput >= 2.0 on every model; T3 part (c) owalnuts-threaded 16/16 ok and owalnuts-threaded/owalnuts wall per gradient geomean <= 1.25. Otherwise UNQUALIFIED with the failed clause.
decision_rule.readme_text_if_qualified: Linux (x86_64, glibc, GCC 13.3, BridgeStan 2.9.0): the default concurrent-replica dispatch is qualified (WP65): 0/500 child faults, draws bit-identical to the serialised path, <A2 range>x gradient throughput at four callers, wall per gradient <C1>x CmdStan's on the fixed-16 (pinned, co-tenanted, one seed).
decision_rule.scope: The qualification covers the measured host class, toolchain, BridgeStan version and run shapes. It says nothing about macOS, aarch64, musl, or Windows; nothing in this study changes a default or library code.
decision_rule.not_gates: A1, A4 and the threaded predictions are predictions, not qualification clauses beyond those named above. Predictions are printed beside the values whether they hold or not.

rules: Preregistration and protocol committed before the first cell. Builds, the manipulation probe and binary smoke runs on a BridgeStan test model (not a study model, no study seed) are infrastructure. Parts run sequentially in the order (a), (b), (c), one process at a time. Report every cell; failures, faults and timeouts are results; no reruns; no tuning after seeing results. A driver killed by the host may be relaunched; launched-but-unrecorded children stay faults/interruptions and are not relaunched; an interrupted (c) cell without an artifact may be rerun once with the same seed, recorded as a deviation. Amendments only for parts not yet run, committed before them.
